stem: What must a proper lookout use to detect and assess nearby vessels?

options.text: Sight, hearing, and all other available means appropriate to conditions

explanation: Rule 5 requires a proper lookout by sight and hearing as well as all available means appropriate to the prevailing circumstances and conditions.

stem: Which best describes safe speed under the navigation rules?

options.text: A speed that produces no wake
A speed allowing proper and effective collision-avoidance action and stopping within an appropriate distance
The local posted limit in all circumstances

explanation: Rule 6 defines safe speed in terms of the ability to take effective action to avoid collision and to stop within an appropriate distance.

stem: When should a mariner treat risk of collision as existing?

options.text: Only if another vessel is within one nautical mile
Whenever there is any doubt about whether the risk exists
Only if both vessels are power-driven

explanation: Under Rule 7, if there is any doubt, risk of collision is deemed to exist.

stem: An approaching vessel remains on nearly the same compass bearing while its range decreases. What does that suggest?

options.text: The other vessel is altering to port
There is no risk if it is far away

explanation: A steady bearing with decreasing range is a classic warning of collision risk; Rule 7 also warns that risk may exist despite bearing change in some circumstances.

stem: How should an avoiding action normally be made when there is room to maneuver?

options.text: As a succession of very small changes
As early, positive action readily apparent to the other vessel
Only after a whistle signal is received

explanation: Rule 8 calls for positive action in ample time; an alteration should be large enough to be readily apparent if circumstances permit.

stem: Which statement best describes an effective course alteration to avoid collision?

options.text: It should be too small to be noticed
It may be substantial if there is sufficient sea room and it avoids a new close-quarters situation
It must always be to port
It must always be accompanied by an increase in speed

explanation: Under Rule 8, a substantial alteration may be most effective when sufficient sea room exists and it does not create another close-quarters situation.

stem: Where should a vessel navigating a narrow channel generally keep?

options.text: As near to the starboard-side outer limit as safe and practicable

explanation: Rule 9 directs a vessel to keep near the outer limit on her starboard side as safe and practicable.

stem: In a narrow channel, which vessel must not impede a vessel that can safely navigate only there?

options.text: A vessel engaged in pilotage duty only

explanation: Rule 9 prohibits a sailing vessel from impeding passage of a vessel that can safely navigate only within the narrow channel or fairway.

stem: A power-driven boat under 20 meters is in a narrow channel. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It may freely impede larger ships
It must not impede a vessel that can safely navigate only within the channel
It always has priority over ships under sail

explanation: Rule 9 specifically limits vessels under 20 meters and sailing vessels from impeding channel-dependent traffic.

stem: When crossing a narrow channel, what must your vessel avoid?

options.text: Crossing at all, under any circumstances
Crossing if doing so would impede a vessel able to navigate safely only in that channel

explanation: Rule 9 prohibits crossing a narrow channel or fairway if doing so impedes passage of a vessel confined to it.

stem: When a vessel must cross a traffic lane in a traffic separation scheme, what heading is generally required?

options.text: As nearly as practicable at right angles to the traffic flow
At the smallest possible angle to the traffic flow

explanation: Rule 10 requires crossing lanes on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow.

stem: When joining a traffic lane from its side, how should a vessel generally enter?

options.text: At right angles to traffic flow
At as small an angle as practicable to the general direction of traffic flow

explanation: Rule 10 directs a vessel entering or leaving a lane from the side to do so at as small an angle as practicable.

stem: Which statement about anchoring in a traffic separation scheme is correct?

options.text: Anchoring is required before joining a lane
Vessels should, so far as practicable, avoid anchoring in the scheme or near its terminations
Anchoring is permitted in all separation zones without restriction

explanation: Rule 10 calls for avoiding anchoring in a traffic separation scheme or areas near its terminations so far as practicable.

stem: Two sailing vessels are approaching with risk of collision and wind on different sides. Which keeps out of the way?

options.text: The vessel with wind on her port side
The vessel with wind on her starboard side

explanation: Rule 12: with wind on different sides, the vessel receiving wind on her port side keeps out of the way.

stem: Two sailing vessels are approaching with risk of collision and wind on the same side. Which keeps out of the way?
explanation: Rule 12: when both have wind on the same side, the windward vessel keeps out of the way of the leeward vessel.

stem: A sailing vessel on port tack sees another sailing vessel to windward and cannot determine her tack. What should it do?

options.text: Keep out of the other vessel's way
Sound one prolonged blast and stop
Assume the other vessel has priority regardless of risk

explanation: Rule 12 specifically requires the port-wind vessel to keep out of the way when uncertain about the tack of a windward vessel.

stem: From what sector must a vessel approach another to be considered overtaking under Rule 13?

options.text: More than 22.5 degrees abaft the other vessel's beam

explanation: Rule 13 defines overtaking as approaching more than 22.5 degrees abaft the beam of the vessel being overtaken.

stem: When does an overtaking vessel's obligation to keep clear end?

options.text: When it sounds the first whistle
When it passes the other vessel's beam
When it is finally past and clear

explanation: Rule 13 says a subsequent bearing change does not convert overtaking to crossing; the obligation continues until finally past and clear.

stem: Two power-driven vessels meet nearly head-on with risk of collision. What is the normal maneuver?

options.text: The smaller vessel stops, the larger continues
Neither alters unless the other signals

explanation: Rule 14 requires each vessel to alter course to starboard so they pass port-to-port.

stem: In a power-driven crossing situation with collision risk, which vessel must keep out of the way?

options.text: The vessel having the other on its starboard side
The vessel having the other on its port side

explanation: Rule 15 gives the keep-clear duty to the vessel with the other on her own starboard side.

stem: In a crossing situation where you are give-way, what should you avoid if circumstances admit?

options.text: Passing astern of the stand-on vessel
Crossing ahead of the stand-on vessel

explanation: Rule 15 directs the give-way vessel to avoid crossing ahead of the other vessel if circumstances admit.

stem: What is a stand-on vessel's initial obligation when Rules 12-17 apply?
explanation: Rule 17(a)(i) generally requires a stand-on vessel to keep course and speed initially.

stem: When may a stand-on vessel act by her maneuver alone?

options.text: Whenever she prefers to pass ahead
When it becomes apparent that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action

explanation: Rule 17(a)(ii) permits action when the give-way vessel apparently is not taking appropriate action.

stem: When must a stand-on vessel act to avoid collision even though she originally had right of way?

options.text: When so close that the give-way vessel's action alone cannot avoid collision
Whenever the vessels are within two miles

explanation: Rule 17(b) requires the stand-on vessel to act when a collision cannot be avoided by action of the give-way vessel alone.

stem: A power-driven stand-on vessel acts in a crossing situation against a vessel on her own port side. Which alteration should she avoid if circumstances admit?
explanation: Rule 17(c) says a power-driven vessel acting in a crossing situation should, if circumstances admit, not alter to port for a vessel on her own port side.

stem: Under Rule 18, which vessel does a power-driven vessel underway generally keep clear of?

options.text: A sailing vessel, unless another rule such as overtaking applies
Every fishing boat with trolling lines

explanation: Rule 18 generally places power-driven vessels below sailing vessels, subject to Rules 9, 10, and 13.

stem: For purposes of the steering and sailing rules, a vessel fishing with ordinary trolling lines that do not restrict maneuverability is generally treated as:

options.text: A vessel engaged in fishing under Rule 3(d)
A vessel restricted in ability to maneuver
A power-driven vessel if propelled by machinery

explanation: Rule 3(d) excludes fishing gear that does not restrict maneuverability, such as trolling lines, from the definition of vessel engaged in fishing.

stem: A pilot boat is proceeding under power while performing pilotage duty. Does that automatically exempt it from normal steering and sailing rules?

options.text: No; it remains subject to the applicable rules for its status and situation
Only if it uses a flashing yellow light

explanation: A vessel engaged on pilotage duty does not receive an automatic right of way simply because of its occupation.

stem: How should a seaplane on the water generally navigate around other vessels?

options.text: Keep well clear of all vessels and avoid impeding their navigation
Claim right of way over power-driven vessels

explanation: Rule 18(e) directs seaplanes on the water generally to keep well clear and avoid impeding vessel navigation.

stem: In restricted visibility, what should a vessel using operational radar do?

options.text: Use radar systematically to determine collision risk
Assume radar removes the need for lookout
Wait for visual contact before making any assessment

explanation: Rule 19 and Rule 7 require systematic assessment, including radar information, where fitted and operational.

stem: You hear a fog signal apparently forward of your beam in restricted visibility and cannot establish that collision risk is absent. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce speed to the minimum at which you can keep course and, if necessary, take all way off
Sound three short blasts and accelerate

explanation: Rule 19(e) requires reduction to the minimum steerage speed, taking all way off if necessary, and navigating with extreme caution.

stem: A power-driven vessel is making way through the water in fog. Which signal should it sound at intervals of not more than two minutes?

options.text: One short and one prolonged blast

explanation: Rule 35(a): a power-driven vessel making way sounds one prolonged blast at intervals not exceeding two minutes.

stem: A power-driven vessel is underway but stopped and making no way through the water in fog. Which signal applies?

options.text: Two prolonged blasts in succession, separated by about two seconds

explanation: Rule 35(b) prescribes two prolonged blasts separated by about two seconds at intervals not over two minutes.

stem: Which fog signal is associated with a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver while underway?

options.text: One prolonged followed by two short blasts
One short and one prolonged blast

explanation: Rule 35(c) covers vessels not under command, restricted in ability to maneuver, constrained by draft, sailing, fishing, and towing/pushing: one prolonged then two short.

stem: For a vessel 20 meters or more in length at anchor in restricted visibility, what bell signal is required?

options.text: Rapid ringing for about five seconds at intervals not exceeding one minute
One prolonged whistle blast every five minutes
Three short whistle blasts every minute

explanation: Rule 35(g) requires rapid bell ringing for about five seconds at intervals not over one minute while at anchor.

stem: What sound-signaling capability is required for a vessel under 12 meters in length?

options.text: A whistle complying with Annex III, always
Some means of making an efficient sound signal

explanation: Rule 33(b) does not require the standard whistle/bell but requires another means of making an efficient sound signal.

stem: At what length does Rule 33 require an additional gong?
explanation: Rule 33(a) requires a gong (or equivalent) in addition to whistle and bell for vessels 100 meters or longer.

stem: What is the duration of a short blast under the navigation rules?
explanation: Rule 32(b) defines a short blast as about one second.

stem: What is the duration of a prolonged blast?
explanation: Rule 32(c) defines a prolonged blast as four to six seconds.

stem: Which whistle signal expresses doubt about another vessel's action in sight of one another?

options.text: At least five short and rapid blasts

explanation: Rule 34(d) permits at least five short and rapid blasts when intentions or sufficient action are in doubt.

stem: What does three short whistle blasts indicate under Rule 34?
explanation: Rule 34(a) uses three short blasts to mean 'I am operating astern propulsion.'

stem: Under the International Rules, one short maneuvering blast indicates:

options.text: I am altering my course to starboard
I am altering my course to port
I intend to leave you on my starboard side

explanation: International Rule 34(a): one short blast means 'I am altering my course to starboard.' Inland passing-signal wording is different.

stem: Under Inland Rules, what does one short passing signal mean when vessels are in sight and maneuvering under Rule 34?

options.text: I intend to leave you on my port side
I am altering my course to port
I intend to leave you on my starboard side

explanation: Inland Rule 34(a): one short blast indicates intent to leave the other vessel on your port side; this differs from the International wording.

stem: Which pair of all-round lights identifies a vessel not under command at night?
explanation: Rule 27(a) specifies two all-round red lights in a vertical line for a vessel not under command.

stem: Which vertical sequence of all-round lights identifies a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver?
explanation: Rule 27(b) specifies all-round red-white-red in a vertical line for a restricted-ability vessel.

stem: Which vertical pair of lights identifies a trawling vessel engaged in fishing?
explanation: Rule 26(b): a vessel engaged in trawling shows green over white all-round lights.

stem: Which vertical pair of lights identifies a vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling?
explanation: Rule 26(c) prescribes red over white all-round lights for fishing other than trawling.

stem: How far around the horizon does a masthead light show?
explanation: Rule 21(a) defines the masthead light as white over an arc of 225 degrees.

stem: What horizontal arc does each sidelight show?
explanation: Rule 21(b) defines each sidelight's arc as 112.5 degrees.

stem: What horizontal arc does a sternlight show?
explanation: Rule 21(c) defines the sternlight as 135 degrees, centered astern.

stem: A power-driven vessel under 12 meters in length may substitute which arrangement for normal underway lights?

options.text: One all-round white light and sidelights

explanation: Rule 23(c)(i) allows one all-round white light and sidelights for a power-driven vessel less than 12 meters.

stem: A sailing vessel under sail is also propelled by machinery. Which day shape normally applies?
explanation: Rule 25(e): a vessel proceeding under sail when also being propelled by machinery displays a cone, apex downward, forward.

stem: A vessel engaged in towing astern has a tow length greater than 200 meters. How many masthead towing lights in a vertical line?
explanation: Rule 24(a): three masthead lights in a vertical line when the tow length, from stern of towing vessel to after end of tow, exceeds 200 meters.

stem: What day shape identifies a vessel aground when required by Rule 30?
explanation: Rule 30(d) prescribes three black balls in a vertical line for aground vessels, subject to small-vessel exemptions.

stem: When in doubt whether a vessel is overtaking, what must you assume?

options.text: That it is overtaking and act accordingly

explanation: Rule 13(c) says if in any doubt whether overtaking, assume it is overtaking and act accordingly.

stem: When navigating near an area of restricted visibility, what must a power-driven vessel have ready?

options.text: Her engines ready for immediate maneuver

explanation: Rule 19(b) requires every vessel to proceed at a safe speed and a power-driven vessel to have her engines ready for immediate maneuver.
